info.text: Session 4a Quiz - Pancreas, Spleen, Nodes and Kidneys

questiontext.text: Dilatation of both the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct is known as the double duct sign and suggests:

generalfeedback.text: This combination warrants prompt evaluation for an obstructing lesion at the pancreatic head or ampulla. Malignancy is the most concerning cause, but benign causes, including stones, chronic pancreatitis, and strictures, can also produce this pattern.

answer.text: An obstructing lesion at the pancreatic head or ampulla warranting prompt evaluation, most concerning for pancreatic cancer but also seen with stones, chronic pancreatitis, or benign strictures
A normal variant in the elderly

questiontext.text: A patient referred for liver screening is found to have a 9 mm CBD and a 5 mm pancreatic duct. The correct action is:

generalfeedback.text: The double duct sign is not a finding to schedule a repeat scan for. It warrants prompt evaluation for an obstructing lesion, malignancy is the most concerning cause, though benign causes such as stones, chronic pancreatitis, or strictures are also possible.

answer.text: Reassure, as the liver is normal
Refer for cross-sectional imaging on the same urgency pathway as a suspicious liver lesion

questiontext.text: In a middle-aged adult, the main pancreatic duct measured in the body of the pancreas is normally about:

generalfeedback.text: About 2 mm in the body is a practical reference, widening somewhat with age; the head and neck can measure more. Record the site, the method and the patient's age.

questiontext.text: Normal pancreatic parenchyma compared with normal liver is typically:

generalfeedback.text: The pancreas is iso- to slightly hyperechoic relative to liver and becomes more echogenic with fatty replacement over time.

answer.text: Similar or slightly more echogenic, becoming brighter with age

questiontext.text: The part of the pancreas most often inadequately visualized is the:

generalfeedback.text: The tail is the hardest region to see, and bowel gas defeats pancreatic imaging more than any other abdominal organ.

questiontext.text: When you measure splenic length, the image should show:

generalfeedback.text: Rotate until the image shows the longest distance between the two poles; that length is what you compare with the height-based table.

answer.text: Both poles of the spleen in one longitudinal plane
The splenic hilum in cross section
The left kidney beside the spleen

questiontext.text: The correct approach for measuring splenic length is:

generalfeedback.text: A left lateral intercostal window with rotation to the true long axis is the accurate technique.

answer.text: Left lateral intercostal, rotated to the maximal longitudinal section between the poles
Right lateral decubitus, anterior probe placement

questiontext.text: Splenomegaly is generally suggested when splenic length exceeds approximately:

generalfeedback.text: About 12 cm is a common general limit, but normal length depends on height and sex; use the height-based table or SplenoCalc (Session 3).

questiontext.text: Which lymph node dimension is most relevant when assessing for malignancy?

generalfeedback.text: Short-axis diameter is the dimension that matters; a long node can be entirely normal.

questiontext.text: A long-to-short axis ratio of less than 2 in a lymph node is:

generalfeedback.text: Oval nodes with a ratio of 2 or more are more reassuring; rounded nodes with a ratio under 2 are a supportive, nonspecific feature raising suspicion. Normal short-axis thresholds also vary by nodal station.

answer.text: A supportive, nonspecific feature, since rounding of a node raises suspicion

questiontext.text: Loss of the echogenic hilum in a lymph node is:

generalfeedback.text: Rounded shape plus loss of the fatty hilum is a useful supportive pairing, though neither feature alone is diagnostic.

answer.text: A supportive, nonspecific concerning feature, particularly combined with a rounded shape
A normal finding in all adults

questiontext.text: Which lymph node stations are most relevant to hepatobiliary and pancreatic malignancy, and already on your scanning route?

generalfeedback.text: You pass through both during the standard protocol, and nodal disease at these stations changes staging.

questiontext.text: A limitation of assessing deep abdominal lymph nodes with the Vscan Air CL is that:

generalfeedback.text: Nodal morphology is a fine-detail assessment; at abdominal depth you lose that resolution, so the threshold to escalate should be lower.

answer.text: Nodes cannot be seen at all
The linear probe cannot reach abdominal depth, so nodal detail is assessed with the coarser curved array

questiontext.text: The primary role of the right kidney in this screening course is as:

generalfeedback.text: The liver-kidney comparison is how steatosis is graded, and both must appear in the same frame. Renal parenchymal disease can alter renal cortical echogenicity and invalidate the comparison.

answer.text: A target organ for cancer screening
The echogenicity reference for grading liver brightness

questiontext.text: Which renal finding during a liver screening study should be documented and referred?

generalfeedback.text: Simple cysts are common and usually incidental; hydronephrosis, gross asymmetry, or a solid mass need referral.

answer.text: A single small simple anechoic cyst
Hydronephrosis with a dilated collecting system
A kidney measuring within normal limits

questiontext.text: A trainee spends ten minutes attempting to image a difficult pancreatic tail and rushes the hepatic dome. This is:

generalfeedback.text: Complete the liver protocol to standard first; the neighbouring organs are context, not the target.

answer.text: A worse study overall, because the liver is the target and dome coverage is the priority
Good practice, since pancreatic cancer is aggressive

questiontext.text: The two features that together distinguish a gallstone from a gallbladder polyp are:

generalfeedback.text: Mobility with repositioning and clean posterior shadowing strongly favor a stone; polyps typically show neither, though small stones may not shadow and mobility should still be confirmed by repositioning.

answer.text: Posterior acoustic shadowing and mobility with repositioning
Color Doppler flow and wall thickness

questiontext.text: Gallbladder wall thickening in a cirrhotic patient with ascites most likely represents:

generalfeedback.text: In this population thickened walls are common and most often secondary. Over-calling cholecystitis on wall thickening alone, without clinical correlation, sends well patients down an acute surgical pathway.

answer.text: Secondary wall thickening, for example from ascites, rather than cholecystitis

questiontext.text: Acute cholecystitis should not be diagnosed on wall thickening alone because:

generalfeedback.text: Wall thickening has a wide differential, including ascites, hepatitis and heart failure. A positive sonographic Murphy sign supports acute cholecystitis, but its absence does not exclude it, including in gangrenous cholecystitis (ACEP Sonoguide).

answer.text: The finding is nonspecific; it must be interpreted with stones, distension, fluid around the gallbladder, the sonographic Murphy sign and the clinical picture
Ultrasound cannot see the gallbladder wall
Wall thickness cannot be measured accurately

questiontext.text: Normal gallbladder wall thickness in a distended, fasting gallbladder is approximately:

generalfeedback.text: Under about 3 mm. Above that opens a differential, most of which is not cholecystitis.

answer.text: Any thickness, as it is not measurable

questiontext.text: A patient with a known intact gallbladder (no previous cholecystectomy) says they ate shortly before the screening study, and the gallbladder cannot be identified. Which explanation must be excluded before reporting anything about stones?

generalfeedback.text: A fasting rescan is required. Stone exclusion is only valid in a fasting, distended gallbladder.

answer.text: Post-prandial contraction - a contracted gallbladder cannot exclude stones

questiontext.text: Imaging the gallbladder in two planes and two patient positions roughly 90 degrees apart is recommended because:

generalfeedback.text: Two planes plus two positions defeat artifact and test stone mobility in one maneuver.

answer.text: A single plane frequently contains an artifact that mimics or hides a stone, and repositioning also tests mobility

questiontext.text: Which part of the gallbladder deserves deliberate attention because an impacted stone there is easily missed?

generalfeedback.text: A stone impacted at the neck is both the easiest to overlook and among the most clinically important.

questiontext.text: A single sessile gallbladder polyp that has grown since the previous scan should be:

generalfeedback.text: Most polyps are harmless cholesterol polyps, but size, sessile morphology and interval growth raise the question of gallbladder malignancy. Current guidance generally considers referral for polyps 10 mm or larger, or 6 to 9 mm with risk factors; growth of 2 mm or more is interpreted alongside current size and risk factors rather than triggering referral on growth alone.

answer.text: Documented with size and morphology, and routed to the referral pathway

questiontext.text: The oblique plane running roughly from the right shoulder toward the umbilicus is used to image:

generalfeedback.text: This oblique plane gives the long axis of the portal vein with the duct running anterior to it.

answer.text: The hilar segment of the bile duct, with the portal vein in long axis

questiontext.text: When the anterior approach to the pancreatic tail fails, a useful alternative is to:

generalfeedback.text: The spleen provides an acoustic window to the tail when bowel gas defeats the anterior route.

answer.text: Use a left intercostal window with the spleen as an acoustic window

questiontext.text: Irregular, beaded 'string of pearls' dilatation of the pancreatic duct is more suggestive of:

generalfeedback.text: Beaded, irregular dilatation suggests chronic pancreatitis; a dilated duct that ends abruptly is the key warning sign for pancreatic cancer.

questiontext.text: Chronic pancreatitis is relevant to a cancer screening course because it:

generalfeedback.text: A mass in chronic pancreatitis can look very similar to pancreatic cancer on B-mode, so any focal mass is referred.

answer.text: Can form a mass that looks very similar to pancreatic cancer

questiontext.text: A normal-appearing pancreas on ultrasound in a patient with severe upper abdominal pain:

generalfeedback.text: Ultrasound can be normal in the early hours. Diagnosis is clinical plus lipase; ultrasound looks for a biliary cause, differentials and complications.

answer.text: Does not exclude acute pancreatitis, which may show no sonographic change early

questiontext.text: The principal role of ultrasound in suspected acute pancreatitis is to:

generalfeedback.text: Diagnosis is clinical and biochemical; ultrasound contributes etiology, differential and complications.

answer.text: Look for a biliary cause, check differentials such as aneurysm, and assess complications

questiontext.text: To follow the pancreatic tail from the body view, the correct approach is to:

generalfeedback.text: The splenic vein does not run flat across the abdomen; it rises toward the splenic hilum and the tail wraps with it. The goal is to keep following the vein toward the hilum, whichever rotation direction achieves that on your device and starting orientation; sliding straight left loses both.

answer.text: Rotate the probe as needed to keep following the splenic vein as it climbs and wraps posteriorly toward the splenic hilum
Slide straight to the patient's left

questiontext.text: The second look at the pancreatic tail is obtained:

generalfeedback.text: The splenic window is part of the pancreatic exam, not just the splenic one, and the anterior route fails often enough that one attempt is not enough.

answer.text: Through the spleen, on a left intercostal view

questiontext.text: The most common unimaged part of the pancreas on ultrasound is the:

generalfeedback.text: Two deliberate looks at the tail, anteriorly along the vein and through the spleen, is the mitigation. Gas in the stomach often hides the tail.

questiontext.text: Which window is correct for measuring splenic length?

generalfeedback.text: Measure from the left side between the ribs, rotating until both poles are in one plane.

answer.text: Left intercostal, with both poles in one plane

questiontext.text: Approximate splenic volume is calculated as:

generalfeedback.text: The additional dimensions are worth taking where a spleen is borderline or where change is being tracked over time.

answer.text: Length x depth x thickness x 0.5

questiontext.text: A spleen that exceeds the probe's field of view should be:

generalfeedback.text: Reporting a measurement you know is truncated is misleading; naming the limitation is not.

answer.text: Documented as exceeding the field, or measured with a panoramic mode if available

questiontext.text: Which gallbladder views does the screening protocol require?

generalfeedback.text: Two planes plus two positions defeats artifact and tests mobility; the neck is where impacted stones hide.

answer.text: No dedicated views unless the patient has symptoms
Long and short axes in the first position and again after repositioning, with a deliberate look at the neck

questiontext.text: Which liver view specifically covers the region most often left unimaged?

generalfeedback.text: The hepatic dome is the classic blind spot, and the intercostal view in partial expiration is what reaches it.

answer.text: Right lobe intercostal, in quiet or partial expiration

questiontext.text: The liver-kidney echogenicity comparison requires:

generalfeedback.text: Judging brightness across separate images taken at different gain settings is a guess, not an assessment.

answer.text: Both organs in the same frame at one gain setting

questiontext.text: If the pancreatic tail cannot be visualized despite both approaches, the correct action is to:

generalfeedback.text: The next reader has no way to know what your study did and did not exclude unless you name the gap.

answer.text: Record that the tail was not visualized and why
Omit the pancreas from the report
